## Summary

- Polish floating comment cards with clearer heading and author typography, consistent avatars, improved spacing, and rounded dashed connectors.
- Improve drag-focus behavior, keyboard access to reactions, reaction-picker sizing, and reply-editor auto-sizing; add focused regression coverage.

## Review status

- Unresolved actionable findings: None
- Residual risks: No known outstanding issues; visual evidence uses a sanitized local seed workspace.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The override selects the DOM factory directly. The traced resize path synchronously rebuilds projections for all draft lines when the wrapping column changes, and the factory constructs live DOM and reads character ranges without reusing previous break data. Duration depends on draft size; no timings were measured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Temporary DOM nodes, HTML and per-character arrays, browser text layout, and Range.getClientRects queries for the entire reply draft.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For one reply editor, whole-draft allocation/layout scales with total draft characters and lines, multiplied by distinct wrapping-column changes during resizing. Identical widths/columns are deduplicated; ordinary edits need not rewrap the entire draft.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased paste/restore latency and renderer-main-thread blocking during interactive horizontal resizing, with additional allocation and GC pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Outside accessibility mode, SimpleCommentEditor used the default simple strategy with the configured editor font. Whole-model wrapping on initialization or width changes used MonospaceLineBreaksComputerFactory rather than live browser DOM measurement.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: All floating replies now use browser-based wrapping regardless of draft size. Full-model initialization and each distinct wrapping-column change allocate and measure a temporary DOM representation of the complete draft.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added wrappingStrategy: 'advanced' at commentReply.ts:107 replaces the normal default 'simple' strategy for every floating reply, including large pasted or restored drafts.
Findings.Title: Bound DOM wrapping for large floating replies
Findings.Impact: Pasting/restoring a lengthy review draft containing logs or code, then dragging the card's horizontal resize handle, now performs whole-draft DOM construction and synchronous layout repeatedly on the renderer input path, causing stalls and dropped resize frames.
Findings.Evidence: ReviewFloatingWidget._onResize calls _setWidth, which calls CommentThreadWidget.layout and CommentReply.layout. ViewModelLines.setWrappingSettings calls _constructLines for changed wrapping columns; _constructLines requests every model line. DOMLineBreaksComputerFactory ignores previousLineBreakData, builds HTML and per-character arrays for all requests, attaches the container to document.body, and discovers breaks through Range.getClientRects (domLineBreaksComputer.ts:29-36, 83-175, 409-472). The reply's capped height does not limit these requests.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep proportional/advanced wrapping for ordinary replies but add a large-draft fallback that switches font and wrapping strategy together to the existing monospace/simple path, or defer expensive large-draft width reflows until the resize settles.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new selector reaches the full-size pseudo-element's blur(12px). Existing drag, resize, and horizontal-scroll paths change its size or sampled backdrop continuously without disabling the filter. Added compositor work is statically established; duration depends on GPU, pixel density, and visible card area.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GPU backdrop sampling, blur passes, and intermediate compositor surfaces for each affected visible card.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Scales with the sum of affected visible cards' physical pixel areas and invalidated frames. Detached cards do not contribute; GPU eligibility does not bound area or card count.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased frame-production cost and dropped drag, resize, or scrolling frames.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Floating cards painted an opaque peekViewResult background and existing shadow, without a card-sized backdrop blur during dragging, resizing, or scrolling.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each eligible visible card now has a live, full-area blur layer that stays enabled during movement and backdrop changes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added floating-widget selector at frostedGlass.css:147 applies the existing full-size backdrop-filter pseudo-element to previously solid comment cards.
Findings.Title: Suspend live card blur during movement
Findings.Impact: With floating comments and Modern UI glass enabled, dragging/resizing a large card over code or horizontally scrolling code behind cards adds repeated full-area filtering, degrading smoothness on high-DPI or lower-powered accelerated GPUs.
Findings.Evidence: frostedGlass.css:155-173 creates a width:100%, height:100% ::before with backdrop-filter:blur(12px), without a motion exclusion. ReviewFloatingWidget's header-drag callback and _onResize call _render; _attach subscribes to both vertical and horizontal scrolling. _render updates overlay placement, while horizontal scrolling changes code underneath cards. Independently expanded widgets have independent materials, without shared filtering or motion suppression.
Findings.Recommendation: Use the solid theme background during dragging/resizing or backdrop scrolling, and restore glass after a coalesced settled notification, preserving existing capability and transparency gates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, restore, update, and close floating or inline comment threads
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CommentController displays newly encountered threads sequentially. Floating display awaits the thread body and reply initialization before attachment, sizing, and showing. Avatar/image downloads do not block that await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire a canonical commentsInput model reference and create/reuse an in-memory Markdown text model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reference acquisition per newly constructed reply editor; provider reuses models by URI. Generated reply URIs normally identify distinct editors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same model-reference acquisition and eager reply construction occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Floating display awaits reply initialization; no filesystem, database, network, or subprocess operation is performed by this registered content provider.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assign a browser-converted avatar URI to an img element; remote URIs can cause an image request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One assignment on initial image construction or actual URI transition, not each comment update. Equal revived URIs are skipped; browser caching may avoid network transfer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Initial images and defined-to-defined URI changes already loaded. This PR also handles absent-to-defined icons; undefined/removal/failure uses a local codicon and does not retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous image loading is off the thread-display await path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct threads after retained-widget deduplication, comments within each thread, reply-capable threads, and changed image URIs. Existing message DOM construction is not virtualized, but this PR does not introduce it.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normal full comment refresh serializes newly displayed threads, with asynchronous image loads overlapping. Independent provider updates can overlap, but replacement/generation checks are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Thread widgets are retained for identical provider thread objects. Model references use canonical URI keys and in-memory provider reuse. Avatar URI equality avoids unchanged reloads; browser image caching is unchanged and there is no new retry/negative-cache loop. The new avatar listener is cleared on replacement/error and disposed with the node.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged model acquisition cardinality and bounded avatar/listener lifetime. Large restored draft wrapping is addressed separately.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Thread/message population and remote image cache behavior vary; no durations were measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression from option propagation, decorative icons, required avatar transitions, or lifecycle handling. A large restored draft reaches the reported DOM-wrapping regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Paste, restore, type into, and horizontally resize a floating reply editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Model projection construction and editor layout execute synchronously on the renderer. Resize calls _setWidth, thread layout, and reply layout; changed wrapping columns reconstruct all model-line projections before resize processing completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build temporary HTML and per-character arrays, append all requested lines to document.body, and synchronously measure character ranges using Range.getClientRects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A full-draft DOM representation on initialization/paste and each distinct wrapping-column change; geometry-query count grows with lines and discovered wrap points. Incremental typing may request only changed lines.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Outside accessibility mode, replies used the default simple/monospace wrapping factory, without live DOM measurement. Full projection reconstruction existed, but its implementation was substantially cheaper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Browser text layout and range measurements block the current renderer operation; not background work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total characters and model lines of one reply draft, affected lines for incremental edits, and distinct wrapping-column changes during horizontal resizing. The visible editor-height cap does not cap the model or wrapping input.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous renderer work for the resized reply; there is no worker or debounce between sash events and the whole-draft measurement. Cost is per distinct wrapping column, not blindly every pointer pixel or every message in the thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unchanged widths and wrapping columns are deduplicated. The DOM factory ignores previousLineBreakData and recreates measurement DOM for changed columns, unlike the prior fast path's ability to reuse prior projection information. Temporary DOM is removed afterward rather than retained.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct option-to-factory selection and the complete resize-to-projection-to-browser-measurement path were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Prevalence and size of long review drafts containing logs/code and actual frame durations are unmeasured; this limits severity rather than the established mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported a medium-severity regression for unconditional browser wrapping of large floating replies. Ordinary short replies and constant-time height calculation do not merit separate findings.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag or resize visible cards, or horizontally scroll code behind them with glass enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Drag callbacks, resize callbacks, and scroll listeners update card geometry; the compositor must then produce the frame. The newly applied full-size material filters the changing sampled backdrop before that frame can be presented.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sample and blur the backdrop through a card-sized backdrop-filter: blur(12px) compositor surface.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One independent full-area material per affected visible card, repeatedly evaluated when its geometry or sampled backdrop changes; no shared surface or motion suppression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cards had opaque theme backgrounds and shadows, without this backdrop-filter surface.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Additional GPU/compositor work lies on frame production during interactive movement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure newly visible code columns through editor rendering and read header geometry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Code extents are cached per line until edits/font/layout/injected text invalidate them. Header midpoint is newly read once per successful attachment measurement, then cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Code-column measurement and its cache already existed. This PR adds only a bounded cached header read, not repeated warm-frame measurement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold geometry may require editor rendering/layout, but warm scrolling reuses extents and the header midpoint.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Affected visible card count, physical pixel area of each card, and invalidated frames. Hidden/collapsed cards are detached. Cards can overlap code after user placement; horizontal code scrolling changes the backdrop even when their horizontal placement stays fixed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each attached widget has its own direct scroll listener. Dragging targets one card; several cards may have changing backdrops simultaneously. Model/content/view-zone notifications are animation-frame coalesced, but scroll/drag updates and compositor filtering have no new global limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Code-line extents have existing invalidation and caching. Header midpoint is cached until reattachment. Connector outline strings are deduplicated as before; the added connector path and min/max scans are bounded by visible range rectangles. No application snapshot or settled-state cache bounds the new live material.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in newly enabled full-area filtering and direct interactive reachability. The cached geometry additions do not independently establish a significant regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GPU speed, device pixel ratio, surface size, overlap, and number of visible cards determine the frame-time impact; no compositor trace was collected.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported a medium-severity regression for leaving live glass active during card movement and changing backdrops. No separate finding for constant-size rounded connectors or bounded cached header measurement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Focus cards, hover truncated titles, open reaction pickers, and toggle a reaction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Focus and menu presentation perform local DOM/style updates. Title geometry is read only when the delayed hover is requested. Toggling a selected reaction awaits its existing controller/extension handler; merely opening the picker does not issue that request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the extension controller's reaction handler through the existing proxy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One proxy invocation per selected reaction activation, independent of menu placement; zero for opening an empty picker, now disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one-call handler path existed before the PR. Changes to DOM placement, menu class, and enabled state do not multiply calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reaction action completion awaits the handler; picker rendering itself is local.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One hovered/focused message or title, the selected comment's reaction options, and actual user reaction activations; not all comments per focus event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local synchronous focus/DOM changes and existing asynchronous user actions. No new fan-out or in-flight requests are introduced. New drag focus invokes the existing body-focus path rather than launching additional model work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reactions are rebuilt using the existing action stores and MutableDisposable ActionBar; old actions and DOM containers are cleared. Delayed hover is registered once and disposed with the header. Menu actions are sourced from the existing reaction group rather than refetched.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged reaction IPC cardinality and bounded hover/action ownership. Extra width reads follow existing measurement and introduce no new write/read loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reaction option counts and extension-handler duration are provider-dependent but their mechanism is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable performance regression. Visual/focus/keyboard behavior changes and suppressed empty menus are not treated as performance fixes without an established expensive prior mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable glass, restore settings, or use an unsupported/reduced-transparency desktop environment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Glass capability initialization is after workbench restoration and does not block comment display. Until supported accelerated compositing is known, cards remain solid. Settings/theme/capability notifications toggle the existing workbench class.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read nativeHostService.isGPUCompositingEnabled and subscribe to GPU compositing changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial read per contribution/renderer plus shared lifecycle notifications, not one read per comment card or layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same capability initialization and subscription already controlled other glass surfaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off comment-display critical path; initial/failed/disabled states preserve solid backgrounds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workbench containers/windows and eligible visible cards after the existing environment, accessibility, CSS-support, and GPU gates; capability reads do not scale with card count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single async initial capability request per renderer; existing synchronous class/style propagation across containers. No introduced process/network burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GPU compositing state is stored by the contribution and updated by existing lifecycle events. No polling or per-card capability lookup is added. Reduced transparency, high contrast, unsupported CSS, and failed/pending GPU state bypass the added material.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the GPU gate and request cardinality are unchanged and bound affected platforms, but do not bound visible material area.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual adoption of the floating-comment and Modern UI settings is unknown; supported lower-powered GPUs remain eligible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new IPC/startup regression. Existing eligibility guards reduce exposure to the reported live-filter issue but do not eliminate its interactive frame-production cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 21 changed files and all diff pages, with targeted caller, cache, lifecycle, browser-layout, model-provider, reaction-IPC, and GPU-gating traces. Submitted two medium-severity introduced regressions: unbounded whole-draft DOM wrapping on interactive reply width changes and live full-card backdrop filtering during movement. Other layout/metadata/action changes were bounded, necessary, or unchanged in expensive-call cardinality. No sufficiently proven removed performance regression warranted blame/fix-learning submission. Static review only; performance magnitudes are unmeasured.
